headline: Corinth Canal Opens, Linking Ionian and Aegean Seas After Centuries of Dream
dispatch: The Corinth Canal was formally inaugurated today, cutting through the narrow isthmus that has divided the Ionian and Aegean seas since antiquity. The waterway, nearly four miles long and carved through limestone cliffs reaching eighty metres high, allows vessels to bypass the long and treacherous voyage around the Peloponnese. Greek and international dignitaries gathered at the northern entrance as the first ships prepared to pass through the newly completed passage.
answer: Corinth Canal formally opened, linking two seas, 1893
